chapter_title: Programmatic Ecosystem: DSP, SSP, Exchange & Ad Server
component_fit_evidence: The Trade Desk Programmatic 101 is a relevant one-hour introduction to ecosystem players, data, identity and privacy. IAB Tech Lab ads.txt, sellers.json and SupplyChain add primary references for seller relationships. Together they support the ecosystem foundation, but do not teach the complete commercial cost stack or all ad-server operations.
material_gaps: Gross-to-net media cost, DSP/SSP/exchange/data/verification fees, publisher/ad-server responsibilities, latency and Indonesia inventory economics need direct operational evidence.
next_action: Map every participant, transaction, data signal, fee, contract owner and control; reconcile gross-to-net cost using a synthetic Indonesia inventory example.

component_fit_evidence: IAB Tech Lab OpenRTB 2.6 documents bid-request and impression objects, deal context and transaction structure; ads.txt, sellers.json and SupplyChain add seller-path transparency. These are primary standards but do not cover every exchange-specific implementation or commercial auction rule.
material_gaps: Auction variants, floors, timeouts, header bidding, deal enforcement, reseller paths, fees and win-rate diagnosis depend on implementation. Seller transparency is not proof of fraud-free inventory.
next_action: Annotate two OpenRTB request/response traces; compare open auction and deal paths, fee layers and authorised sellers; show how exchange rules affect clearing price, timeout and win rate.

component_fit_evidence: The Trade Desk course introduces programmatic data, identity and privacy. Google Consent Mode clarifies that tags respond to a consent choice already collected by a site/app; UU PDP 27/2022 provides Indonesian processing-ground principles. These sources support boundaries, not every DSP/browser identity scenario.
material_gaps: Identity graphs, browser restrictions, match-rate measurement, data provenance, contextual vs behavioural targeting, cross-border processing and legal basis per purpose need specialist platform and local privacy review.
next_action: Build a data-source/identity matrix with owner, purpose, legal basis, consent state, match-rate limitation, retention and activation controls. Test denied-consent and contextual-only cases; do not equate Consent Mode with legal permission.

component_fit_evidence: OpenRTB provides format/impression objects relevant to banner, video, audio, native and DOOH transaction context. Google Ad Manager deal comparison and DV360 Programmatic Guaranteed clarify Google-specific reservation and delivery behaviour, not a neutral cross-publisher inventory catalogue.
material_gaps: CTV/audio/native/in-app/DOOH specs, scale, measurement eligibility, suitability, commercial terms and local publisher availability require format- and seller-specific documentation.
next_action: Compare six inventory types on audience context, supply, creative specs, device, deal availability, measurement, quality and net cost. Mark Google-specific behaviour separately and verify Indonesian inventory availability.

component_fit_evidence: The Trade Desk and StackAdapt routes introduce DSP ecosystem concepts; DV360 line-item documentation provides an exact operating object. These remain vendor-specific, and a learning course does not guarantee a live buying seat or partner access.
material_gaps: Exact DV360 hierarchy, advertiser/partner permissions, account prerequisites, Amazon DSP comparison and a safe lab environment are not fully mapped. Tool access must not be implied by course completion.
next_action: Create a synthetic DV360 hierarchy from partner/advertiser through campaign, insertion order and line item, covering naming, targeting, budget, flight, creative, permissions and QA. Distinguish demo from production access.

component_fit_evidence: DV360 line-item setup and CM360 placement-tag documentation cover important trafficking objects; CM360 macro reference supports URL/tag QA. These are primary for Google's stack but not a complete vendor-neutral trafficking SOP or contractual approval hierarchy.
material_gaps: Approved IO/brief and live platform settings remain authoritative; a trafficking sheet is a control register, not a contract/system of record. Creative specs, redirects, macros, consent and deal QA differ by vendor and placement.
next_action: Reconcile signed IO/approved brief, DSP line item, CM360 placement/ad/creative, click URL, macro, tag and deal ID. Include wrong landing page, duplicate tracker, broken redirect and rejected creative cases.

component_fit_evidence: DV360 documentation explains budget hierarchy, pacing modes and frequency caps, including how insertion-order limits constrain line-item delivery. It is operationally relevant, but these controls should not be generalised to every DSP.
material_gaps: Bid shading, auction pressure, win-rate/clearing-price diagnosis, conversion-signal quality and commercial bid/budget trade-offs need further evidence. DV360 pacing/caps are product-specific.
next_action: Extend the pacing simulator with flight and daily budgets, IO/line-item caps, win rate, floor, CPM, reach/frequency and signal quality. Require a reasoned change log with underdelivery, overspend and fatigue scenarios.

component_fit_evidence: Google Ad Manager compares deal types and DV360 Programmatic Guaranteed documentation describes proposal acceptance, contracted quantity and publisher-side pacing. This supports the guaranteed vs non-guaranteed distinction, but is platform/contract specific.
material_gaps: Buyer/seller seat compatibility, deal IDs, private-auction floors, fixed prices, priority, underdelivery, makegoods, cancellation and billing need full commercial examples and buyer-side workflow evidence.
next_action: Build a three-deal comparison with IDs, price/floor, dates, format, targeting, guarantee, volume, delivery and escalation. Reconcile activation with signed terms and platform acceptance.

chapter_title: Brand Safety, Viewability, IVT & Supply Quality
component_fit_evidence: IAB Tech Lab ads.txt/sellers.json/SupplyChain support seller-path transparency. MRC viewability and IAB/MRC attention standards define measurement boundaries. They reinforce that seller authorisation, viewability, attention, brand safety/suitability and IVT are separate constructs.
material_gaps: Supply-chain files do not certify human traffic, viewability or suitability. Viewability is not attention; vendor IVT/brand-suitability methodology, coverage, exclusions and Indonesia inventory measurement remain unvalidated.
next_action: Create a 10-seller scorecard with authorised path, duplication, fees, IVT, viewability, suitability, attention, vendor coverage, sample bias and remediation owner. Keep each metric separate.

component_fit_evidence: CM360 documentation defines Floodlight counting options (Every, One per user, One per session) and conversion windows; Google Consent Mode explains tag behaviour under consent states. These are primary for Google implementation but not a neutral DSP/GA4 reconciliation framework.
material_gaps: Attribution windows/models, click/view-through rules, timezone, reporting latency, redirects, identity, consent and deduplication require a common event dictionary and cross-platform reconciliation case.
next_action: Build an event-to-report matrix across DSP, CM360/Floodlight and GA4: event definition, source, timezone, window, counting, consent, dedupe key and lag. Do not call attributed conversions incremental lift.

component_fit_evidence: DV360 pacing/frequency documentation and TTD learning provide operational inputs for delivery analysis; MRC/IAB standards constrain quality metrics. No single mapped source teaches a complete commercial post-buy with fee-adjusted outcomes and causal incrementality.
material_gaps: Full cost-to-outcome reconciliation, margin, reach deduplication, incrementality, holdout design and alternative explanations need additional statistical/financial sources. ROAS alone is insufficient.
next_action: Add synthetic post-buy data for spend/fees, delivery, reach/frequency, quality, conversions, margin and holdout; reconcile denominators and limits. Record changes, evidence, counterfactual and follow-up test.

component_fit_evidence: TTD course, OpenRTB, seller-transparency standards, DV360 operating documentation and CM360/Floodlight references jointly cover major supply, activation, trading and measurement components. These are source components, not an integrated validated answer/capstone.
material_gaps: Integrated worked case, synthetic auction/fee data, buyer-seller terms, trafficking evidence, measurement assumptions and a reproducible rubric are not provided by the learning routes. Live buying access must not be implied.
next_action: Build one SIMULATED advertiser case connecting objective, audience, supply path, deal, DSP configuration, trafficking, pacing, quality, Floodlight/GA4 reconciliation, risks and executive decision; have a trader/measurement SME grade it.
